ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a right circular cylinder, with upper and lower circular bases parallel to each other; the lateral surface is a curved cylindrical surface, and there are no polygonal flat side faces. Reasoning: The problem asks which cross-sectional shape cannot appear when this cylinder is cut by a plane. When the plane is parallel to the base, the cross section can be a circle; when the plane cuts the cylindrical lateral surface obliquely, the cross section can be an ellipse; when the plane cuts parallel to the axis of the cylinder, the cross section can be a rectangle. Since a cylinder has no oblique flat side face that can form four straight sides and only one pair of opposite sides parallel, a trapezoidal cross section cannot be obtained.
